name: Walt Disney Concert Hall
notes: Modelled in SketchUp (24 Sep 2026) and read back as meshes: the stainless-steel sails as closed curved sheets, each an arc in plan rising and curling outward at the top (cubic flare), their top edges tilting and bowing; ten petals round a low steel roof over the hall, the lower three curling out over the glass lobby at the entrance corner, and the drum as a petal curled into a ring. On a limestone podium with the stair on its east side. From the article's one exterior (the entrance corner at dusk) and general knowledge of the building; the plan, the backs of the sails and all heights (tallest ~46 m) are estimates, and the entrance corner is faced south-east rather than to the real street grid. Garden trees kept from the first version. Refined 24 Sep 2026 (three rounds; the SketchUp meshes untouched, only what is round them): the garden trees had stood at street level inside the 6 m podium, so only their crowns showed through the stone; they now stand in a planted garden on the podium top (the real hall's garden is up on its podium) - a soil bed with lawn, a low stone parapet, shrubs and a white blob for the tiled 'Rose for Lilly' fountain - drawn before the meshes so the sails always win; streets round the podium (asphalt with a white lane line) on the front, back and side, with a row of street trees along the front that stops short of the entrance corner, which photo 01 shows open. The garden's position follows the model's rotated plan, not the real one (on the real site it lies to the south-west). Refined 28 Oct 2026 in SketchUp (three rounds, each built by scripts/sketchup/walt_disney_concert_hall.py, read back, converted and previewed; the article's photo 01, the entrance corner at dusk, is still the one exterior). The five biggest mismatches, most important first: (1) the hall read as a bouquet of thin petals round a bare dome of steel, with the sky seen through it, where photo 01 shows a dense stack of overlapping sails; the dome is gone and the hall is a steel-clad block (22 m, its top drawn in) the sails stand against; (2) the two tall rear sails of photo 01 (one near-flat sheet about 27 m wide, a second leaning back about 20 m wide, a glass slot between them, the tallest corner about 46 m) were missing: they are two near-flat sheets facing the entrance corner, with the glass slot; (3) the sails beside them stood as tall as the rear ones: the side petals come down to 24, 22, 14 and 14 m, the front blades go up to 22-30 m, so the tall sheets stand clear above the lower layers as in the photograph; (4) the drum east of the entrance was a ring with a cap; it is a smooth oval barrel about 22 m across and 28 m high, its top drawn back and in, with a long low curved wall before it (the building's name is on that wall in the photograph; no letters are drawn); (5) the voxel was 0.9 m and the model 33,000 dots, over the 25,000 the pass keeps to: it is 1.1 m (23,000 dots) and every sheet is 1.2 m thick so none falls between the voxel columns. Still guessed: the plan (a rotated rectangle of 42 x 16 m behind the sails, the sails' places round it) and the backs of the sails (the photograph shows one side only), the heights of the lower layers (read off photo 01 at about 9 px a metre), the lobby, which the photograph shows at street level to the left but which stands on the 6 m podium here, and the ring that the petals still make round the court: the real sails do not close round the hall. The .skp in sketchup/ is rebuilt.
